Tomás Reyes  9:14 AM
Hey — I'm enrolling in the HDHP this week as a single filer and I want to confirm the HSA employer contribution. The public handbook says $100/month for individual. Is that still current?

Alex (People Ops)  9:21 AM
Good timing Tomás — that figure is stale. Effective April 1, 2026 the HSA employer contribution for Team Member Only (individual) on the HDHP went up to **$125/month**. The old $100/month number is still sitting in the us-benefits-overview handbook page but it's outdated. PlanSource is already applying the new amount. Family/dependent tier also changed separately (see slack-003 from a couple weeks back).

Tomás Reyes  9:23 AM
Perfect, thanks. $125 × 12 = $1,500/yr from GitLab then.

Alex (People Ops)  9:24 AM
Correct. And that's still pre-tax at the federal level — CA/AL/NJ residents pay state tax on it.

Naomi Halverson  11:02 AM
Expecting in October and starting to plan my leave. The handbook says 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Want to confirm before I tell my manager.

Alex (People Ops)  11:18 AM
Huge congrats Naomi! Quick correction — effective **April 1, 2026** GitLab Paid Parental Leave was extended from 16 weeks to **20 weeks** of fully paid leave. The parental-and-other-leave handbook page still lists 16 weeks because the MR hasn't merged yet (tracking in gitlab-com/content-sites/handbook#2903). Everything else is the same: still up to 3 segments, still must be used before the child's 1st birthday, still 100% of weekly wages, still submit to Tilt 30–45 days before leave.

Naomi Halverson  11:20 AM
That's amazing news. So 20 weeks paid, not 16. Anything else I should flag?

Alex (People Ops)  11:23 AM
Just the duration changed. Pay, segmentation, and the F&F Day +4 bonus are all unchanged. I'll DM you the Tilt intake link.

Question on corporate card receipts. I had a $62 client dinner on my Navan card last week. US team member. Handbook says receipts required for US charges over $50, so I uploaded it. Just want to double-check I did the right thing.

Alex (People Ops)  2:51 PM
You did the right thing by uploading it Wesley, but heads-up: the US receipt threshold was raised from **$50 to $75** effective **March 20, 2026** (Finance announcement in #whats-happening-at-gitlab). Your $62 charge actually wouldn't have required a receipt under the new rule — but uploading is never wrong. The corporate-card-policy handbook page still says $50 because the MR is pending.

Wesley Park  2:53 PM
Good to know. So single US charges ≤ $75 are now receipt-free?

Correct — ≤ $75 no receipt needed for US team members. Still must upload within 30 days for anything over $75. Missing Receipt Affidavit still applies if you lose one.

Hey — just got promoted to Director and trying to understand my bonus cadence. Handbook says Director+ bonuses are paid twice per year (semi-annual). Is that still accurate?

Q2 payout lands mid-July after the quarter closes. You'll get a calendar invite from Total Rewards with the exact date.

I got summoned for jury duty next month and the notice says potential 4-week trial. Handbook says up to 25 working days paid. Just want to confirm in case it runs long.

Thanks for flagging Harper. Update: the paid jury-duty / legal civic obligation cap was raised from **25 to 30 working days** effective **March 25, 2026**. So I have up to 6 weeks of paid jury duty coverage now. That's a big relief.

Can I expense ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro on my personal card? Both are ~$20/mo. I use them daily for work.

Good question Rami. We published an **AI Tool Use policy on April 5, 2026** (not yet in the public handbook — internal only until legal review closes). **No customer data, no unreleased source code, no personnel data** in any prompt. Summaries, public docs, and your own work-in-progress writing are fine. Full policy link is in #ai-tools-guidelines. Violations are reviewed by Security.

Iona Grimaldi  3:12 PM
My team wants to buy a specialized design tool — annual cost is about $18k. Do I need to go through an RFP or is that below the threshold?

Alex (People Ops)  3:19 PM
Hi Iona — $18k/year is under the **$25k RFP threshold**, so **no competitive bids are required**. You just submit a Zip request through Okta for a new purchase request and Procurement will route it through the standard reviews (Security, Privacy, Legal, FP&A). Timeline is usually 5 days to 3 weeks depending on whether the vendor is new and how responsive their counsel is.

Iona Grimaldi  3:21 PM
Great — and if we wanted to expand to $30k next year?

Alex (People Ops)  3:24 PM
At $25k–$100k you'd need a **business-led quick-bid with 2 vendor bids**. $100k–$250k is 2–3 bids business-led. Over $250k is Procurement-led with 5+ bids. Exact table is in the procurement handbook page.

metadata.title: Do I need an RFP for an $18k software purchase?

Solene Marchetti  8:48 AM
I'm traveling to São Paulo next week for a customer meeting. If there's a medical emergency, who do I call?

Alex (People Ops)  8:56 AM
Great that you're thinking ahead Solene. Use **International SOS (ISOS) 24/7 Assistance: +1 215 942 8226**. Also download the **ISOS Assistance App** before you leave and register with your GitLab email (use a unique password — not your GitLab credentials). ISOS covers medical emergencies, security situations, claims assistance for the Business Travel Insurance Policy, and pre-trip health advice.

Solene Marchetti  8:58 AM
Perfect. Is the coverage automatic or do I need to enroll?

Alex (People Ops)  9:01 AM
**Automatic and year-round** — no enrollment. Coverage includes emergency medical up to $250k per occurrence and security evacuation. Family members traveling with you are also covered (spouse, domestic partner, children under 26). Email is philadelphia@internationalsos.com if you can't get through on phone.

metadata.title: Who do I call for a medical emergency while traveling?
